message.content:
I'm planning a new feature for KasirKu (Next.js 16 POS app). User wants:
1. A printable "shift closing settlement report" (like Moka POS's shift-close report) showing cash totals, QRIS totals, and EDC (card machine) totals separately — printed to a thermal printer at shift close.
2. A printable "menu sales report" (which menu items sold, quantities) — also printable.
3. BOTH reports need to be printable filtered by a date/date-range of transactions, not just "this shift" — i.e. a cashier or owner should be able to pick a date and print either report for that date.

I need you to report back (under 500 words) on the exact current state of relevant code, since a LOT changed today in this same session (git history: printer retry queue, receipt printing via native Bluetooth/LAN, POS local-first architecture, checkout parallelization):

1. Payment methods: grep for "QRIS", "EDC", "Kartu", "BUILTIN_PAYMENT_METHODS" across src/ — what are the actual payment method strings used today at checkout (pos-screen.tsx and wherever payment method is selected)? Is "EDC" a distinct method anywhere, or would it need to be added as a new built-in/custom payment method? Check `custom_payment_methods` table usage too.

2. `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/shifts/page.tsx` — what does the shift history list show today? Is there already ANY print/report button on shift rows? (Note: an earlier now-reverted session commit had added a `/shifts/[shiftId]/receipt` route with payment-method + per-menu report — that commit was fully reset out via git reset before this current session's work started, so it likely does NOT exist in the current codebase — please confirm whether it exists or not.)

3. `supabase/migrations/20260702100900_shift_rpc.sql` (or wherever close_shift RPC lives) — what fields does the close_shift RPC compute today (cash_sales, non_cash_sales, etc.)? Does it break down by payment method beyond cash/non-cash, or would a settlement report need its own query against `transaction_payments` grouped by method?

4. `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/reports/page.tsx` — this page already showed "Metode Pembayaran" and "Menu Terlaris" breakdowns with date-range filters (Hari Ini/7 Hari/Bulan Ini/Semua/Kustom) when tested earlier today. Read this file fully: what queries does it run, what date-filtering mechanism does it use (URL search params? component state?), and is there an existing CSV/Excel export action already wired up (I recall "⬇️ Ekspor Data" buttons)? This is likely the best foundation to extend with a PRINT option, reusing its date-filter and data-aggregation logic rather than building parallel logic.

5. `src/lib/escpos.ts` and `src/lib/receipt-print.ts` — confirm current exports (buildKitchenTicket, buildReceiptTicket if it still exists, buildReceiptBuffer) so I know what ESC/POS ticket-building patterns already exist to reuse for two NEW ticket types (settlement report ticket, menu-sales report ticket).

6. `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/transactions/[transactionId]/receipt/print-button.tsx` and `reprint-kitchen-button.tsx` (in the same transactions/[transactionId] folder) — confirm the current pattern for a "print to configured printer" button (server action builds KitchenPrintJobPayload[], client calls dispatchPrintJobs from @/lib/dispatch-print-jobs) so a new report-printing feature follows the same established pattern.

Report concrete facts with file paths and relevant code snippets/line numbers. Don't propose a design — I'll do that myself using your findings.

1	import type { SupabaseClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
2	import { buildReceiptTicket } from "./escpos";
3	
4	export type BuildReceiptBufferResult =
5	  | { success: true; buffer: Buffer }
6	  | { success: false; error: string };
7	
8	// Shared by the automatic "print receipt on checkout" path (checkout()) and
9	// the manual "Cetak ke <printer>" button on the receipt page — both just
10	// need the priced ticket bytes for a transaction, independent of which
11	// printer it ends up going to.
12	export async function buildReceiptBuffer(
13	  supabase: SupabaseClient,
14	  businessId: string,
15	  transactionId: string,
16	): Promise<BuildReceiptBufferResult> {
17	  const [{ data: business }, { data: transaction }, { data: items }, { data: payments }] =
18	    await Promise.all([
19	      supabase.from("businesses").select("name").eq("id", businessId).single(),
20	      supabase
21	        .from("transactions")
22	        .select(
23	          "invoice_number, date, subtotal_raw, service, tax, total_item_disc, order_disc_amt, total, voided, cashiers!transactions_cashier_id_fkey(name)",
24	        )
25	        .eq("id", transactionId)
26	        .eq("business_id", businessId)
27	        .single(),
28	      supabase
29	        .from("transaction_items")
30	        .select("id, name, price, qty")
31	        .eq("transaction_id", transactionId)
32	        .order("id", { ascending: true }),
33	      supabase
34	        .from("transaction_payments")
35	        .select("method, amount, received, change")
36	        .eq("transaction_id", transactionId),
37	    ]);
38	
39	  if (!business || !transaction) {
40	    return { success: false, error: "Transaksi tidak ditemukan." };
41	  }
42	
43	  const buffer = buildReceiptTicket({
44	    businessName: business.name,
45	    invoiceNumber: transaction.invoice_number,
46	    date: new Date(transaction.date).toLocaleString("id-ID", { dateStyle: "medium", timeStyle: "short" }),
47	    cashierName: (transaction.cashiers as unknown as { name: string } | null)?.name ?? "—",
48	    voided: transaction.voided,
49	    items: (items ?? []).map((i) => ({ name: i.name, qty: Number(i.qty), price: Number(i.price) })),
50	    subtotal: Number(transaction.subtotal_raw),
51	    itemDiscount: Number(transaction.total_item_disc),
52	    orderDiscount: Number(transaction.order_disc_amt),
53	    service: Number(transaction.service),
54	    tax: Number(transaction.tax),
55	    total: Number(transaction.total),
56	    payments: (payments ?? []).map((p) => ({
57	      method: p.method,
58	      amount: Number(p.amount),
59	      received: p.received === null ? null : Number(p.received),
60	      change: p.change === null ? null : Number(p.change),
61	    })),
62	  });
63	
64	  return { success: true, buffer };
65	}

content.text: Now let's check the `period.ts` for date-filter mechanism and settings.tsx for custom_payment_methods context.

Have enough. Compiling the report now.

## Findings

**1. Payment methods** (`src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx:91`):
```js
const BUILTIN_PAYMENT_METHODS = ["Tunai", "Kartu", "QRIS"];
```
Merged with per-business `customPaymentMethods` (line 150) fetched from the `custom_payment_methods` table (`src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/page.tsx:90`, `.from("custom_payment_methods")`, business-scoped rows with a `name` column; insert/delete in `settings/actions.ts` lines 21 & 43). **"EDC" does not exist anywhere** as a distinct method — "Kartu" is the closest existing built-in. There is no separate EDC concept; it would have to be added either as a new built-in string or a custom payment method row. Same `BUILTIN_PAYMENT_METHODS` set is duplicated in `ticket-pos-screen.tsx`.

**2. Shifts page** (`.../shifts/page.tsx`): Only a read-only history list (last 50 closed shifts) showing cashier, total, opened/closed time, tx count, expected cash, difference, void count, notes. **No print/report button of any kind exists on shift rows.** Confirmed via filesystem: `shifts/[shiftId]/` directory does not exist at all (`ls` on it failed) — the earlier receipt route is indeed gone, not present in current tree.

**3. `close_shift` RPC** (`supabase/migrations/20260702100900_shift_rpc.sql:53-133`): computes only `cash_sales` (method = 'Tunai') vs `non_cash_sales` (method != 'Tunai') — a binary split, plus `total_sales`, `expected_cash`, `difference`, `tx_count`, `void_count`. **No per-method breakdown** (QRIS vs Kartu vs custom methods aren't separated). A settlement report needs its own query against `transaction_payments` grouped by `method`, filtered by `shift_id` (or by date range), same pattern the reports page already uses.

**4. `reports/page.tsx`**: Server component, date-filtering via **URL search params** (`period`, `from`, `to`) parsed by `parsePeriod`/`getPeriodRange` in `reports/period.ts`, with a cookie (`kk_period`) persisting the last choice. Single query at lines 92-101 pulls `transactions` with nested `transaction_items` and `transaction_payments`, filtered with `.gte("date", fromIso)`/`.lt("date", toIsoExclusive)`. It aggregates in-memory: `byMethod` map (lines 144-152, "Metode Pembayaran" donut) and `menuSales` map (lines 166-186, "Menu Terlaris" list) — both already exactly the aggregations needed. Custom period form posts via plain GET (lines 216-246). Export section (lines 484-506) already has three working links: `.../reports/export?type=menu&...`, `.../reports/export?type=transactions&...`, and `.../export?...` (Excel) — all CSV/Excel, no print action yet, but same query-param convention (`periodQuery`) could gate a new print link/route.

**5. `escpos.ts`**: exports `buildKitchenTicket` (no prices) and `buildReceiptTicket` (priced, single transaction) — both push raw ESC/POS bytes with `RECEIPT_WIDTH = 32` and a `padLine`/`truncate` helper. `receipt-print.ts` exports `buildReceiptBuffer(supabase, businessId, transactionId)`, which fetches one transaction + items + payments and calls `buildReceiptTicket`. No settlement/menu-report builders exist yet — new ones would follow this same file/function shape.

**6. Print button pattern** (`print-button.tsx`, `reprint-kitchen-button.tsx`): both are `"use client"` components that call a **server action** (`buildReceiptPrintJob`/`buildKitchenReprintJobs` in `transactions/[transactionId]/actions.ts`) returning a `KitchenPrintJobPayload`-shaped job, then call `dispatchPrintJobs(businessId, jobs)` from `@/lib/dispatch-print-jobs` client-side, tracking per-printer `state` (idle/sending/ok/error) in `useState`. `print-button.tsx` also does `window.print()` as a fallback/browser-print path guarded by a `printed` ref to avoid double-fire, and gates the native-printer buttons behind `Capacitor.isNativePlatform()`.
